recipes.title: Sunday Pancakes

ingredients.item: melted butter, plus extra for the pan
Maple syrup and berries, to serve

steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt together in a big bowl.
In a jug, whisk the milk, egg and melted butter until smooth.
Pour the wet into the dry and stir gently until just combined. A few lumps are fine — don't overmix.
Let the batter rest for 5 minutes while you heat a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Brush the pan with a little butter and pour in about ¼ cup of batter per pancake.
Cook until bubbles pop on the surface, about 2 minutes, then flip and cook 1 minute more.
Keep warm in a low oven while you cook the rest. Serve with maple syrup and berries.
recipes.notes: The first pancake is always the chef's. Double the batch and freeze the extras between sheets of baking paper.

recipes.title: Weeknight Bolognese
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the onion and carrot and cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Turn up the heat, add the mince and cook, breaking it up, until browned all over.
Stir in the tomato paste for a minute, then add the chopped tomatoes, oregano and half a tin of water.
Simmer gently for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and rich. Season to taste.
Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti in plenty of salted boiling water. Save a mug of pasta water before draining.
Toss the pasta through the sauce, loosening with pasta water if needed. Serve with parmesan.
recipes.notes: Sneak in a grated zucchini with the carrot — nobody has noticed yet.

recipes.title: Grandma's Chicken Noodle Soup
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot. Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook gently for 10 minutes.
Pour in the stock, add the chicken thighs and bay leaves, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks, and return it to the pot. Fish out the bay leaves.
Add the noodles and simmer for 6–8 minutes until tender.
Stir through the parsley, season well, and serve in your biggest bowls.
recipes.notes: Grandma swears by a squeeze of lemon in each bowl. She is right.

recipes.title: Chewy Oat Cookies
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line two trays with baking paper.
Beat the butter and brown sugar together until pale and fluffy.
Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, bicarb and salt, then fold through the oats and chocolate chips.
Roll into walnut-sized balls and place on the trays, leaving room to spread. Flatten slightly.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until golden at the edges but still soft in the middle.
Cool on the tray for 5 minutes (the hardest step), then move to a rack.
recipes.notes: Pull them out while they still look a little underdone — that's the secret to chewy.
